summary: (a) browser now resolves from the host Playwright install via packages/cli/src/witness/browser.ts, with a named witness.browser-not-provisioned refusal raised in operator/witness.ts and counted by the census; (b) script-surface and runtime-script-observation raise named source-absent conditions instead of ENOENT, so offline verify survives a missing work dir (Spike B TRUE, narrowed: static half reconciled against trust/script-surface.json, network half still fully re-derived); (d) pipeline-owned stage dirs declared in the write set; (e) crawl journey named port-free. Clean worktree gate: interventionCount 0, terminalClassification proven, idempotent across two runs, witness digest identical. (c) vendored tarball installs and the CLI loads standalone, but trust:ingest/schema reject a file: lock coordinate and 11 sealed receipts embed the old link:../witness provenance.
open_questions: May packages/trust/src/ingest.ts and packages/trust/src/schema.ts learn about non-registry lock coordinates so a file:vendor tarball can be named rather than rejected? Both are outside this contract and trust:ingest calls lockPackages directly, so the in-contract auditableLockText filter in verify.ts/generate.ts cannot reach it.
Vendoring pulls mitt@3.0.1 into the audited closure, so the SBOM needs a fresh consented OSV ingest before trust:generate will run. Is that refresh authorised, and under which consent id?

Rewriting provenance.ts to read the vendored tarball changes the provenance block embedded in ~11 sealed witness receipts (papercups, hospitalrun, linkfree, memos, killedbygoogle v3, react-boilerplate zero-SW, fuxa, next-killedbygoogle). Re-publishing them means re-running sealed drivers, which this packet forbids. Does the owner want the drivers re-run, the receipts re-sealed by another route, or @async/witness published instead?
